q: 1. Closed traverse is suitable in the survey of
explain: A closed traverse, which returns to its starting point, is suitable for surveying areas that form a closed loop, like the boundary of a pond/lake; rivers, roads and coastlines are elongated features better surveyed by open traverses.

q: 2. The co-ordinate of a point measured perpendicular to the parallel is called
explain: The perpendicular distance of a point from a reference meridian, measured parallel to the parallel (east-west), is called the meridian distance (or total departure) of that point.

q: 3. Total latitude of a point is positive if it lies
explain: By convention, latitude is taken as positive (northing) when the point lies north of the reference parallel, and negative (southing) when south.

q: 4. The altitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude of a traverse leg = length x cosine of its reduced bearing, since latitude is the projection along the north-south meridian direction.

q: 5. If the angular measurements of a traverse are more precise than its linear measurements, balancing of the traverse, is done by
explain: The Transit rule is used to balance a traverse when angular measurements are considered more precise/reliable than the linear measurements, since it corrects latitudes and departures independently in proportion to their own magnitudes rather than the total leg length.

q: 6. The projection of a traverse line on a line parallel to the meridian is known as ... of the line
explain: As per the book's printed answer key, this projection (onto a line parallel to the meridian) is designated departure in this text, though standard convention typically calls this the latitude - readers should verify against their copy.

q: 7. A traverse survey can be plotted
options: by rectangular coordinates or plotting by tangents
by paper protractor or by included angles
by parallel meridian method or plotting by chords
explain: All the mentioned methods are valid ways to transfer field traverse data onto paper.

q: 8. In a transit theodolite error due to eccentricity of verniers is counteracted by
options: reading different parts of main scale
taking both right swing and left swing reading
explain: The error due to eccentricity of verniers (misalignment of the vernier scale centre with the instrument's rotation axis) is counteracted by reading both verniers (typically 180 degrees apart) and averaging the results.

q: 9. Which of the following methods of theodolite traversing is suitable for locating the details which are far away from transit stations?
options: by measuring angle to the point from at least three stations
by measuring angles to the point from at least two stations
by measuring angel at one station and distance from other
by measuring distance from two points on traverse line
explain: Distant details, which cannot be directly chained, are located by the method of intersection, measuring angles to the point from at least two known theodolite stations.

q: 10. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For a precision theodolite traverse suitable for roads and railways, the permissible angular error of closure is 1 minute multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 11. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by
options: L = Latitude x secant of reduced bearing
L = Departure x cosecant of reduced bearing
explain: The length of a traverse line can be computed from its latitude and departure using any of several equivalent trigonometric relations, hence any one of the above methods gives the correct length.

q: 12. An angle of deflection right, may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read
explain: To directly obtain a deflection angle right, the theodolite is set to read 180 degrees when backsighted to the previous station, so that the forward reading directly gives the deflection angle.

q: 13. Which of the following errors can be eliminated by taking mean of both face observations?
options: Errors due to eccentricity of verniers
Errors due to imperfect adjustments of plate levels
Errors due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the mean of face left and face right observations eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perfectly perpendicular to the horizontal axis, since this error reverses sign between the two faces.

q: 14. Which of the following error is not eliminated by the method of repetition of horizontal angle measurement?
options: Error due to eccentricity of verniers
Error due to displacement of station signals
Error due to wrong adjustment of line of collimation and trunnion axis
explain: The method of repetition eliminates errors due to inaccurate graduation and instrumental maladjustments by accumulating readings around the circle, but it does not eliminate the error due to eccentricity of verniers.

q: 15. In order to measure the magnetic bearing of a line, the theodolite should be provided with
explain: To measure the magnetic bearing of a line using a theodolite, a small tabular or trough compass must be fitted onto the instrument.

q: 16. Which of the following doesn't involve the method of traversing?
explain: Per this text, tacheometric surveying is identified as not typically involving the specific method of traversing, unlike chain, theodolite, and plane table surveying.

q: 17. The levelling head of a transit theodolite consists of
explain: The leveling head is the entire lower assembly that connects the instrument to the tripod and includes the screws and plates used to level the device.

q: 18. Size of a theodolite is specified by
explain: The 'size' (e.g., a 10 cm theodolite) refers specifically to the graduated diameter of the lower horizontal circle.

q: 19. The upper plate
options: is attached to the inner spindle and is called vernier plate
has two vernier 180° apart for reading the horizontal angles
is also called alidade of theodolite
explain: The upper plate (vernier plate) carries the verniers and the standards for the telescope and rotates on the inner spindle.

q: 20. If the image formed by the objective of the telescope is not in the plane of cross hairs it is called
explain: Parallax occurs when there is apparent movement between the image and the crosshairs due to the image not falling exactly on the diaphragm plane.

q: 21. The trunion axis or transverse axis is
options: the axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a vertical plane
the axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a horizontal plane
is also known as line of collimation
explain: The trunnion axis is the horizontal axis supported by the standards, allowing the telescope to rotate vertically (transit).

q: 22. 'SPIRE TEST' is used in permanent adjustment of theodolite for
explain: The Spire Test (or Horizontal Axis Test) ensures that the horizontal axis is perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 23. A traverse deflection angle is
options: the difference between the included angle and 180°
explain: The deflection angle is the angle between the extension of the previous line and the current line; it is calculated as 180° - Included Angle.

q: 24. The bearing of the traverse line is calculated by
explain: Bearings can be computed from known starting bearings using either the measured included angles or the deflection angles.

q: 25. The included angle of the theodolite traverse, are generally measured
options: clock wise from the back station
clock wise from the forward station
anti clock wise from the forward station
anti clock wise from the back station
explain: Standard practice is to sight the back station, set zero, and turn clockwise to the forward station.

q: 26. In a closed traverse by included angles, the sum of measured interior angles should be equal to
explain: The formula for the sum of interior angles of a polygon with N sides is (2N - 4) × 90°.

q: 27. The closing error is given by
explain: By Pythagoras' theorem, the magnitude of the closing error is the square root of the sum of the squares of the latitude and departure errors.

q: 28. In a traverse, the algebraic sum of the deflection angles, taking the right hand deflection angles as positive and left hand deflection as negative, should be equal to
explain: In a closed traverse, the sum of the deflection angles must equal 360° to return to the original direction.

q: 29. In closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: As noted in Q332, the total turn required to close a loop is a full circle (360°).

q: 30. In a closed traverse, the closing error should not be more than
explain: Errors in angles tend to accumulate in proportion to the square root of the number of stations (√N).

q: 31. If the sum of northing of a traverse exceeds the sum of southing by 2m and sum of easting exceeds the sum of westing by 2m, the resulting closing error will be
explain: Error = √(ΣL² + ΣD²) = √(2² + 2²) = √8 = 2√2 m.

q: 32. The perpendicular distance of the mid point of the line from the reference meridian is known as
explain: Meridian distance of a line is the distance of its midpoint from the reference meridian.

q: 33. In order to measure a horizontal angle more accurately than a vernier, a
options: method of deflection angles is used
method of double observations is used
explain: The method of repetition allows an angle to be accumulated multiple times on the circle before final reading, effectively refining the measurement precision beyond the vernier's least count.

q: 34. The process of turning the telescope of a theodolite over its supporting axis through 180 in a vertical plane, is called
explain: This action - rotating the telescope through 180 degrees over the horizontal (trunnion) axis - is known by any of the equivalent terms: transiting, reversing, or plunging.

q: 35. The latitude and departure of a traverse line are both positive when the whole circle bearing of the line lies in the
explain: For a WCB in the first quadrant (0-90 degrees, north-east direction), both the latitude (northward) and departure (eastward) components are positive.

q: 36. An angle made by a survey line with the prolongation of the proceeding line, is known as
explain: This angle, formed between a survey line and the prolongation (extension) of the previous line, is by definition the deflection angle.

q: 37. When internal angles are to be subtended by a thedolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: For internal angles to be correctly measured and used in a closed theodolite traverse, the traverse should be run in a counter-clockwise direction.

q: 38. Resolving power of a telescope depends on
options: the pupil aperture of the eye
the diameter of the object glass
explain: The resolving power of a telescope primarily depends on the diameter (aperture) of the object glass (objective lens); a larger objective diameter gives better resolving power.

q: 39. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by
options: L = Latitude x Secant of reduced bearing
L = Departure x Cosecant of reduced bearing
explain: All three formulas given are mathematically equivalent ways of computing the length of a traverse line from its latitude, departure, and reduced bearing - so any one of the above can be used.

q: 40. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) must equal 360 degrees, corresponding to one complete traverse around the figure.

q: 41. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5 exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In precision traversing, included angles are measured by setting the vernier to somewhere near (not exactly) zero when backsighted, and reading both verniers to average out eccentricity errors.
